payload.source_label: Assign heterogeneous material properties to each cell by averaging parameters over its volume

contract.statement: This contract is audited only under the coordinator-selected interpretation under the broad user objective; it is not a literal detailed user reply or a printed-source hypothesis. Choice Q8, selection SHA-256 cfde240a9dda9a58be99f85369b43e99003b0024c7147a33ffa8b071ca7dcf34, row packet SHA-256 aaefcc144aeefcef600cf39053fd6fb40c748de39de966fadf4da247fa04d66e. Original source-only contract SHA-256 5ac1715d6848aeafe3806880a6b9533b6b7d2b901d9eb1256d5d2e2cb815e8bd. Original source account: The source explains that finite volume methods suit heterogeneous media because each grid cell can receive its own material properties through appropriate averaging of material parameters over that cell's enclosed volume. It does not specify the material-averaging formula or assert algebraic laws for an averaging operator. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, Section 1.4, first paragraph.] Earlier, the source explicitly defines the cell average of the solution q as its cell integral divided by cell volume, but does not explicitly make that definition the required material-averaging prescription. [Raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2, first paragraph.]
assumptions: The described application uses finite volume grid cells for a heterogeneous medium. This is the setting of the methodological claim, rather than a separately stated theorem hypothesis. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, Section 1.4: 'a natural choice for heterogeneous media']

Heterogeneous media may have slowly varying parameters or sharp material interfaces with parameter jumps; the discussion does not restrict material variation to one of these cases. [Raw PDF page 29, printed page 7, Section 1.4, final paragraph: 'slowly varying' and 'sharp interfaces between different materials']

The enclosing discussion concerns linear wave problems and presents high-resolution finite volume methods based on Riemann problems as a potentially attractive alternative for the interface problems described. [Raw PDF page 29, printed page 7, Section 1.4 heading and final paragraph; raw PDF page 30, printed page 8: 'For these problems']

The adjacent interface discussion allows a discontinuity in the medium and in initial data at x = 0, with reflected and transmitted waves represented through the interface Riemann solution. This supplies application context, not an averaging identity. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, Section 1.4, first paragraph: 'The idea of a Riemann problem is easily extended']

Conservation form is not a universal standing assumption for the variable-coefficient problems under discussion. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, Section 1.4, second paragraph: 'may not be in conservation form']

Coordinator-selected interpretation: Select normalized integration over each physical cell volume, with the relevant integrability and positive finite volume conditions. Preserve the possibility of other model-dependent averaging rules. Heterogeneous inputs need not yield unequal cell averages.

Material parameters describe the medium, while assigned material properties belong to individual grid cells; neither collection is given a symbol, dimension, or mathematical type. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, Section 1.4: 'material properties' and 'material parameters']
